Jeremiah Ajayi. Marketing consultant for B2B SaaS and technology companies, based in Lagos.

I studied how to win an argument.

Now I help good products win theirs.

Eight years of positioning, launches and content for companies in fintech, HR tech, AI and media. Before that, a law student who couldn’t stop writing. Now also the co-founder of EmpowerQ.

The story so far

The chapters a summary skips.

012017 to 2018

The life I planned

In 2017 I finished secondary school as class valedictorian, headed for Law at Obafemi Awolowo University. I come from a family of lawyers, so the dream felt natural. It was also easy to explain.

While I waited months for the university to resume, I started a blog called Better Than Good, just to write and publish something that was mine. It was my first brush with SEO. Then, in 2018, a friend introduced me to freelance writing, and I saw that words could become work.

022018 to 2021

Law student by day, freelancer by night

I interned at the Securities and Exchange Commission and two law firms, but freelance work kept pulling me elsewhere. When strikes and the pandemic closed the campus, I kept writing, pitching and staying in touch. Kelechi Udoagwu, whom I first contacted in 2019, later hired me as Content and Community Manager at Week of Saturdays, where I started to understand B2B SaaS marketing.

In 2020 I became a UN Millennium Fellow and started Digivention, which helped 1,200+ young Nigerians build digital skills. In 2021 I sent Victor Eduoh a note about his guides on product-led storytelling and asked for a coffee chat. He turned it into a job offer at VEC Studio.

032022 to 2023

The bet

In early 2022 I joined PiggyVest. Months later, Stears offered me a senior content marketing role just as OAU resumed for my fourth year. I could finish Law, or follow the career I had already started building. I chose Stears, and some people thought I had lost my mind.

Then came Nigeria’s 2023 election. Our results tracker ranked first on Google, above the BBC, CNN and INEC, and reached 1.9M+ people. The best marketing, I learned, makes something useful easy to find, understand and trust.

Small proof compounds. Nothing is truly wasted when you are paying attention.

042023 to 2026

Starting again, and going global

Leaving OAU left a gap that mattered to me. In 2023 I went back to school, studying Business Management at Miva Open University while working full-time.

At RemotePass, a Dubai-based HR and payroll platform, I led GTM for launches across EMEA, North America and APAC. Some went out in English and Arabic on the same day; one partnership reached 270+ media outlets. The work took me to more than ten countries.

Then I led product marketing at Xofu, an AI visibility platform, and started publishing my own research on how AI assistants choose which brands to recommend.

See the work →

05Now

Opening doors I had to find my own way through.

In 2025 I co-founded EmpowerQ, a nonprofit working on economic inclusion for LGBTQ+ professionals in Nigeria. It takes what I learned pitching my way into global work and makes that path open to more people.
